title: Godot vs Unity - Vibe Coding
author: Appropriate-Cod7548
selftext: Which of them would you prefer? Target games is shooter and Arcade-like games.

comments.author: No-Difference629
comments.body: Unity is very good with MCP

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: Godot. It's because sources are available and AI would know for sure, if something is a bug of engine, rather then a bug of a code

replies.author: Weareallscrubs
replies.body: Is this a big problem? I don't really understand engine bugs and how often they occur.

comments.author: BadassMinh
comments.body: Pick what fits better for your purpose not what is strictly better. Describe your game and detailed mechanics to AI, discuss with it and ask it which engine fits the best for your game

replies.author: unfamily_friendly
replies.body: Bad idea. AIsays "Unity" because it's just more popular and a lot of big games using it. That doesn't makes Unity better, but makes AI biased. What they should do, is to pick engine based on what they already know (python? C#? Turbo Pascal and cobol?) and if nothing - then what fits better for AI. Because AI will do all the labor

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body: Mine chose Godot, I was looking for more lightweight and customizable

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body: I’ve been having some pretty in depth conversations about the goals of my games and what is important to me about the development, the systems, the size of the games, customizability. So far out of 3 games I’ve nearly finished it built a custom html5 engine for a side scrolling shooter, it used phaser 3 for another and three.js for another. My most recent one is bigger in scope and I’m working on a custom pathing solution so it recommended Godot and building my own custom plugin so I’m going to use it to r&d my idea then see where I’m at.

replies.author: evelyn-chevalier
replies.body: mine chose godot after i explicitly described in detail what im looking for so maybe you should try working with less baseless assumptions

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: Godot is very light to run and easy to learn and use.

comments.author: Weareallscrubs
comments.body:
My own experience was starting with godot, but I'm currently changing to unity because there just aren't that many ai tools for gdscript. It would also be possible to write c# in godot, but I'm not sure how well the ai would handle godot only with c#, so I decided to switch to unity. Not totally sure if working with unity could have some unexpected problems.

Actually I would be thankful if someone has experience with both godot + only c# (or mostly c#) and unity. Which has more potential problems?

replies.author: Upstairs-Mulberry365
replies.body: Godot source is open and gpt handles gdscript very well

replies.author: Weareallscrubs
replies.body: I meant that there aren't that many ready made tools for ais working with gdscript. At least I've had problems finding many tools, for example used for code navigation, that support gdscript.

replies.author: Upstairs-Mulberry365
replies.body: What do you need exactly? I might have some answers for you

replies.author: Weareallscrubs
replies.body: My biggest need are navigation and information tools like codegraph, gitnexus and pi-lens (I'm using pi). I'm only finding very rudimentary code-navigation tools for gdscript, but nothing that would be enough without building something major on top of it.

comments.author: Keln
comments.body:
I have worked with both, I were a Unity game dev for 10 years, in the last year I kept using Unity but I've decided to test Godot due to **Unity slowness in**:

\- Building time (even with good assemblies setup, Godot wins here by 3x speed minimum).

\- Handling testing of stuff, screenshots, the testing framework, etc.

\- Not being able to run Unity in headless or in multiple windows at the same time.

All these three issues were fixed by going to Godot, where I could just run agents freely and they themselves manage multiple PRs agents in worktrees with even 5 or more features being worked and tested in headless/screenshots from running builds or frame by frame analysis at the same time.

Once Unity 7 comes out with the new CoreCLR stuff, I'll try back since it is supposedly improving most of this stuff.
